title: Antiviral Signaling and Innate Immune Networks in Penaeid Shrimp: WSSV‐Centered Evidence and Aquaculture Health Management
content:
This review integrates WSSV-centered evidence on viral recognition, signaling, RNA interference, and cellular and humoral defenses in penaeid shrimp, while defining limits to cross-species inference. Translating these insights into breeding, diagnostics, functional feeds, RNAi interventions, and biosecurity requires functional validation and demonstrable benefits for disease control and production.


ABSTRACT

Viral disease constrains penaeid shrimp aquaculture by destabilizing production, animal welfare and aquatic food-system resilience. White spot syndrome virus (WSSV)-penaeid shrimp models provide the strongest mechanistic evidence for antiviral immunity, but they cannot serve as universal proxies for RNA viruses, decapod iridescent virus 1 (DIV1), crayfish, crabs or freshwater prawns. This review treats crustacean antiviral immunity as an evidence-weighted network rather than a catalog of immune genes, distinguishing study-level evidence for host defense from the separate maturity of proposed aquaculture applications. We integrate Toll/immune deficiency (IMD)–nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), stimulator of interferon genes (STING)–interferon regulatory factor (IRF)–Vago–Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), RNA interference (RNAi), recognition-entry duality, cellular clearance, antimicrobial peptides, and prophenoloxidase (proPO)-linked defense into interacting signaling and innate immune networks. The central conclusion is that pathway biology becomes useful for practical aquaculture when it yields molecular markers and management interventions for validation against diseases and production outcomes rather than simply stronger immune activation.
